chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Ibn Bukayr, from his father, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding a eunuch who deceived a Muslim woman, so she married him.

He said: Separation would be effected between the two of them if the woman so desires it, and his head would be pained, and if she is pleased with it and stays with him, it would not be for her, after her agreement with it, that she refuses him.

key_terms.يُوجَعُ رَأْسُهُ: His head is pained (idiom for financial compensation/damages)

ai.seo_question: What is the marital ruling if a eunuch marries a woman by concealing his condition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the fiqh of 'gharar' (deception) in marriage, specifically regarding a eunuch concealing his impotence, establishing the woman's right to annul the contract or retain it with compensation. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that if the wife consents to remain after discovering the defect, the marriage becomes binding and irrevocable on those grounds, reflecting the balance between contractual transparency and marital stability.
